domain: Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) — being the source LLMs/AI chatbots cite for Central Oregon real estate
summary: The auditor was directionally right that this is a genuinely built-out AEO layer, but it undersold the enforcement and missed two real defects. It reported ONE mechanical gate (G39 ci:ai-crawler-access); there are TWO — it never found scripts/check-ai-structured-data.mjs (G34), a ~25-surface structured-data presence gate wired into ci:gates, which also proves FAQ/Dataset coverage is far wider than the "city and housing-market only" claim (buildMarketFaq is consumed by 7 page files including communities, neighborhoods, and search presets, plus a separate buildPresetFaq). Two defects the auditor did not find: (1) every listing detail page emits DUPLICATE realEstateListing + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, because app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx:560 renders MetadataBlock AND the ListingDetailShell it renders emits its own MetadataBlock at line 128; (2) middleware.ts:163 hard-403s Bytespider while app/robots.ts:48 explicitly Allows it — the robots allow-list is decorative for any bot the middleware screens, and G39 checks only robots.ts, never middleware.ts. The auditor's single highest-priority finding holds and is worse than stated: the AI-referral pipeline runs daily (vercel.json:124, snapshot-channels 0 12 * * * → marketing-snapshot-ga4), and the admin analytics page already loads getGA4SummaryCached — whose return value carries the aiReferrers array in memory — and throws it away without rendering it.

items.requirement: /llms.txt (and ideally /llms-full.txt) content map for AI crawlers
items.evidence: app/llms.txt/route.ts (121 lines, not 122) — dynamic GET, revalidate=3600 (line 7), awaits getRecentBlogPosts({limit:25}) / getPublishedGuides(50) / listMarketReports(12) (lines 21-24) plus getEventsForIndex / getVenuesForIndex / getTrailsForIndex and the static GOLF_COURSES registry. I resolved every URL family it emits against the filesystem: /reports, /reports/explore, /housing-market/reports, /price-drops, /open-houses, /central-oregon/{events,venues,trails}, /communities, /cities, /guides, /blog, /tools/{mortgage-calculator,appreciation,rental-property-calculator}, /homes-for-sale, /contact, /team, /lp/central-oregon-golf — all 19 exist as real app/ routes. Gate: scripts/check-ai-crawler-access.mjs lines 62-79 assert 8 markers including the three DAL function names. Wired at package.json:157 and inside ci:gates (package.json:171). No app/llms-full.txt exists; the only repo mention of llms-full is an unbuilt line item in docs/GROWTH_ACTION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md:102. Middleware does NOT screen this route — the matcher at middleware.ts:532 excludes any path containing a dot, so /llms.txt bypasses bot screening entirely.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Confirmed partial, and the auditor's gate critique is correct: check-ai-crawler-access.mjs is a source-text marker check, so all three DAL fetchers returning [] via their resilient-cache fallback would still pass CI while serving a curated-pillars-only file. Adding what the auditor missed: /llms.txt is not referenced from app/sitemap.ts, app/robots.ts, or any <link rel> in app/layout.tsx — discovery depends purely on crawlers guessing the convention. No llms-full.txt.
items.why_it_matters: llms.txt is the most direct machine-readable signal to answer-engine crawlers. The route is real and its links resolve; llms-full.txt is a completeness gap, not a functional one.

items.requirement: robots.txt allows AI/LLM crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bytespider, Applebot-Extended)
items.evidence: app/robots.ts is 53 lines (auditor cited 16-53 — correct). Wildcard rule allows ['/', '/api/og'] (line 25) — the auditor missed the /api/og carve-out for social unfurlers. 20 explicit per-bot Allow rules at lines 28-49. G39 (scripts/check-ai-crawler-access.mjs:31-43) enforces a 10-bot required list and an Allow-of-'/' regex, wired into ci:gates. BUT: middleware.ts runs a second, independent screen that G39 never inspects. middleware.ts:154-155 GOOD_BOT_RE bypasses googlebot/bingbot/applebot/gptbot/oai-searchbot/chatgpt-user/perplexitybot/claudebot/claude-searchbot/claude-web/anthropic-ai/ccbot/google-extended. middleware.ts:162-163 BAD_BOT_RE returns a 403 for 'bytespider' — a bot app/robots.ts:48 explicitly Allows. Four more bots robots.ts Allows are absent from GOOD_BOT_RE: 'Perplexity-User' (the regex token is 'perplexitybot', which does not substring-match 'Perplexity-User'), 'YouBot', 'meta-externalagent', 'Amazonbot'. These fall through to the geo screen at middleware.ts:210-212, which 403s CN/HK/RU/SG by default (middleware.ts:169).
items.gap: [CORRECTED: auditor called this "have" with "None found — this is a strong, actively-gated posture". It is not. app/robots.ts:48 Allows Bytespider and middleware.ts:163 hard-403s it — the two files directly contradict each other, and G39 only reads robots.ts, so CI is blind to the contradiction. Perplexity-User, YouBot, meta-externalagent, and Amazonbot get no GOOD_BOT_RE bypass and are subject to the CN/HK/RU/SG geo block; Meta and Amazon both egress from Singapore. The auditor read robots.ts in isolation and never opened middleware.ts, which is the file that actually decides whether a crawler gets bytes.]
items.why_it_matters: A robots.txt Allow that the edge middleware overrides is worse than no allow-list — it looks correct in the gated file while the crawler gets a 403. The gate that exists (G39) cannot catch this class of regression because it never reads the enforcing file.

items.requirement: Structured data (JSON-LD) coverage across page types — RealEstateListing, Place, Organization, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, Dataset, etc.
items.evidence: Both systems the auditor named are real: components/JsonLd.tsx rendered at app/layout.tsx:120 (import at line 13), and lib/site/json-ld.ts's buildJsonLd driving MetadataBlock. What the auditor missed entirely is scripts/check-ai-structured-data.mjs — gate G34, wired as ci:ai-structured-data inside ci:gates (package.json:171) — which mechanically requires structured-data markers on ~25 named surfaces: layout, about, team, cities/[slug], communities/[slug], cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug], ListingDetailShell, blog/[slug], lib/structured-data.ts (dateModified specifically), area-guides, schools, parks, subdivisions/[slug], zip/[zip], guides/[slug], LeadLandingPage, mortgage-calculator, lp/bend, SearchPageJsonLd, search/[...slug], price-drops. DEFECT the auditor missed: listing detail pages emit every schema TWICE. app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx builds breadcrumb (line 500) + realEstateListing (line 514) and renders <MetadataBlock schemas={listingJsonLdSchemas}/> at line 560, then renders <ListingDetailShell> at line 578 — and ListingDetailShell.tsx builds its own breadcrumb (line 93) + realEstateListing (line 99) and renders <MetadataBlock schemas={schemas}/> at line 128, unconditionally. Two SingleFamilyResidence nodes and two BreadcrumbList nodes per listing page. components/listing/ListingJsonLd.tsx is confirmed dead: the only repo references are docs/ and .auto-memory/ files (docs/SITE_SPEC.md:137 still asserts it is "verified — both imported and rendered", which is false), plus its own default export at line 34.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: three things. (1) The auditor missed G34/ci:ai-structured-data, a wired ~25-surface gate — it reported "a CI gate (G39)" as the only mechanical protection, understating enforcement by half. (2) It missed the duplicate-JSON-LD defect on the site's highest-volume page family; two conflicting SingleFamilyResidence nodes per page is an actual correctness bug, not a completeness gap. (3) Its "blog/guides have no FAQPage" framing is careless: check-ai-structured-data.mjs's guides entry explicitly requires generateBlogSchema and states a hard-coded FAQPage whose Q&As do not appear on the rendered page "violates Google policy and the no-fabrication rule". Absence of FAQPage on guides is a deliberate, code-documented anti-fabrication decision, not an oversight. The auditor's dead-ListingJsonLd finding is confirmed, and docs/SITE_SPEC.md:137 + docs/SEO.md:91 are stale docs still pointing at it.]
items.why_it_matters: Duplicate contradictory schema nodes can suppress rich results and give answer engines two competing claims about the same property. And the stale docs actively misdirect a future editor to the dead file.

items.requirement: Content structure for extraction — Q&A sections, definitional statements, cited stats with dates/sources on market report and city pages
items.evidence: lib/site/market-faq.ts's buildMarketFaq is consumed by SEVEN page files, not two: app/housing-market/[...slug]/page.tsx, app/housing-market/page.tsx, app/housing-market/central-oregon/page.tsx, app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx, app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx, app/communities/[slug]/page.tsx, app/search/[...slug]/page.tsx. A second builder, lib/site/preset-faq.ts's buildPresetFaq, adds FAQ depth to the ~320 indexable search preset pages (required by check-ai-structured-data.mjs's search/[...slug] entry). components/site/FAQBlock.tsx is additionally rendered on app/sell, app/buy, app/join, app/about, app/team, and components/site/golf/GolfFaq.tsx. Both FAQ builders carry unit tests (lib/site/market-faq.test.ts, lib/site/preset-faq.test.ts). Dataset dateModified is wired to the real refresh timestamp, not now() — lib/site/json-ld.ts:131 documents the rule and line 339 emits input.dateModified. Coverage is gated: G34 requires the literal token 'buildMarketFaq' on cities, communities, and neighborhood pages, so removing the FAQ fails CI.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor wrote "This pattern (buildMarketFaq + FAQBlock) is confirmed only for city and housing-market geo pages." That is wrong — it is on communities, neighborhoods, the housing-market hub, central-oregon, and search preset pages too, and it is CI-enforced on three of those. The auditor grepped too narrowly and understated the strongest part of the build. The genuine residual gap is narrower than stated: app/subdivisions/[slug]/page.tsx is the one geo family with NO buildMarketFaq consumption (G34 requires only MetadataBlock there), so subdivision pages get Place + BreadcrumbList but no verified Q&A or Dataset.]
items.why_it_matters: This is the strongest part of the AEO build and it is broader and better gated than the first audit reported. Subdivision pages are the one geo tier still shipping without extractable Q&A.

items.requirement: Entity consistency layer — consistent NAP, sameAs links, Organization schema with brokerage license numbers
items.evidence: components/JsonLd.tsx imported at app/layout.tsx:13 and rendered at line 120 — every page. Organization node typed ['RealEstateAgent','LocalBusiness'] (line 63), telephone CONTACT.phoneDirectTel (line 70), GeoCircle areaServed with Bend midpoint 44.0582/-121.3153 (lines 74-75), PostalAddress (line 79), sameAs: SOCIAL_PROFILES (line 86), WebSite node with SearchAction pointing at /homes-for-sale?keywords= (lines 93-101). Broker sub-entities are RealEstateAgent (line 40) carrying identifier {PropertyValue, propertyID:'Oregon Real Estate License', value: b.licenseNumber} (lines 49-50), sourced from getBrokers() (line 14) with a .catch(() => []) fallback at line 57. G34's first CHECK entry requires the literal 'JsonLd' token in app/layout.tsx, so removal fails CI.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Confirmed have. Every cited line number checks out. One nuance the auditor did not flag: getBrokers() is wrapped in .catch(() => [] as Broker[]) at line 57, so a DAL failure silently drops the founder/employee sub-entities (and therefore every Oregon license identifier) while still emitting the Organization node — a degraded-but-valid render with no error surface. Low severity, worth knowing.
items.why_it_matters: This is the anchor entity AI engines attribute citations to, and it is both live on every page and CI-gated.

items.requirement: Measurement of AI referral traffic (ChatGPT/Perplexity/etc. referrers) in GA4 or visitor_sessions
items.evidence: lib/ai-referrers.ts exports classifyAiReferrer (line 51) and isAiReferrer (line 65), unit-tested in lib/ai-referrers.test.ts including host-boundary and source/medium-form cases. Consumed at app/actions/ga4-report.ts:4, with a dedicated GA4 runReport in the Promise.all at line 115 and classification at lines 364-372. app/api/cron/marketing-snapshot-ga4/route.ts:176 sums it and lines 178-183 write scope='account' metric='ai_assistant_sessions' plus one scope='source' row per engine. Reachability CONFIRMED: vercel.json:124-125 registers /api/cron/snapshot-channels on "0 12 * * *", and that route fans out to /api/cron/marketing-snapshot-${p} for 9 platforms including 'ga4' (app/api/cron/snapshot-channels/route.ts:28, 57). UI: a repo-wide grep for ai_assistant_sessions returns exactly two hits, both inside the cron route. A grep for perplexity|chatgpt|ai referral|aiReferrer|assistant_sessions across app/admin, app/dashboard, and components returns ZERO matches.
items.gap: [VERIFIED — and worse than stated] Confirmed partial. Adding what the auditor missed: the admin analytics surfaces ALREADY load this data and discard it. app/admin/(protected)/analytics/_lib/queries.ts:15,80, app/admin/(protected)/analytics/social/page.tsx:22,286, and app/admin/(protected)/reports/lead-flow/page.tsx:43,231 all call getGA4SummaryCached, whose return type includes the aiReferrers array (app/actions/ga4-report.ts:78). The engine breakdown is in memory on three admin pages and rendered by none of them. This is not "needs a new panel" — it is a discarded field. Also confirmed: no crawler-side measurement exists at all. GPTBot appears in exactly two files repo-wide (app/robots.ts, scripts/check-ai-crawler-access.mjs) — nothing logs AI-crawler user-agent hits, so there is no way to know whether the bots we allow are actually fetching pages.
items.why_it_matters: This is the metric Matt named. The referral half runs daily and is invisible; the crawl half is not instrumented at all. Highest-priority gap, and the referral fix is smaller than the first audit implied.

items.requirement: Freshness signals — dateModified in schema, lastmod in sitemap, present and accurate
items.evidence: app/sitemap.ts is 478 lines (auditor said 479). Confirmed lastModified: now on the entire staticPages block — I counted 39 consecutive entries from line 60 through line 120 alone (homepage, listings browse, luxury, communities, cities, team, blog, guides, all central-oregon hubs, schools, parks, all four housing-market hubs, open-houses, activity, about, contact, sell, valuation, all six buy/sell sub-LPs, golf, lp/bend, lp/tetherow, our-homes, videos, resources, faq, pulse). Blog freshness IS real and gated: lib/structured-data.ts:108-111 sets datePublished from post.published_at and dateModified from post.updated_at ?? post.published_at, and check-ai-structured-data.mjs has a dedicated CHECK requiring both the 'dateModified' and 'generateBlogSchema' tokens in that file. Listing schema freshness gap CONFIRMED by reading the builder end-to-end: lib/site/json-ld.ts case 'realEstateListing' spans lines 221-262 and emits name/description/url/address/geo/numberOfRooms/numberOfBathroomsTotal/floorSize/lotSize/yearBuilt/offers/image/listingAgent — no dateModified, no datePublished. Those two keys appear in the file only at lines 339 (dataset) and 361-362 (article).
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Both halves confirmed by direct read. The now()-stamping is even broader than the auditor's "~60 URLs" estimate implies once the dynamic listing/city/zip/subdivision sections are included, and per-listing schema genuinely has zero freshness field. Correcting one hedge: the auditor wrote the listings table "almost certainly" carries a ModificationTimestamp column — per the rules I did not query, and docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md should be the source consulted before anyone builds this; do not treat "almost certainly" as verified.
items.why_it_matters: A sitemap where nearly every URL claims to have changed at request time is a degraded signal, and the highest-volume page family carries no freshness marker exactly where inventory turns over fastest.

items.requirement: Runtime verification that the AEO surfaces actually serve (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD render in SSR HTML)
items.evidence: Both AEO gates are static source-text checks. scripts/check-ai-crawler-access.mjs uses readFileSync + string .includes() and a regex over app/robots.ts (lines 50-65) and existsSync + marker matching over app/llms.txt/route.ts (lines 62-79). scripts/check-ai-structured-data.mjs is documented in its own header (lines 15-18) as "a PRESENCE check (does the page emit structured data via the approved path), not a deep schema validator" — it greps page source for import/usage tokens. Neither fetches a URL, parses rendered HTML, or validates a JSON-LD payload. No AEO assertions found in any smoke suite.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor never raised this as its own requirement — it noted the llms.txt runtime hole in passing inside item 1 and did not notice the same hole applies to the entire structured-data gate.] Both gates pass on a page that imports MetadataBlock and then renders nothing citable — an empty schemas array, a DAL returning [], or a runtime throw swallowed by a resilient cache all ship green. There is no post-deploy check that /robots.txt, /llms.txt, or any JSON-LD block returns 200 with real content.
items.why_it_matters: Per this repo's own memory on gate drift, a gate that verifies source text rather than served output can sit dark for weeks. The entire AEO layer's enforcement is source-shaped, so its most likely failure mode is invisible.

items.requirement: Conversational / long-tail answer content — direct-answer copy targeting the questions people actually ask AI assistants about Central Oregon real estate
items.evidence: The verified-stat FAQ machinery (buildMarketFaq, buildPresetFaq) generates market-stat Q&A only, and by design produces no question when a stat is null. app/faq/page.tsx exists and is in the sitemap (app/sitemap.ts:119). components/landing/LeadLandingPage.tsx renders a visible FAQ from config.faq with matching FAQPage JSON-LD (required by check-ai-structured-data.mjs). Blog and guides carry BlogPosting/Article schema via generateBlogSchema, with FAQPage deliberately excluded on guides per the anti-fabrication rule in the same gate.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor did not cover this requirement at all — it treated AEO as a markup-and-plumbing problem and never asked whether the site answers the questions an AI assistant is actually asked.] Every gated FAQ surface is stat-driven and geo-scoped. Nothing systematically covers the non-numeric long-tail an assistant fields — process questions, Oregon-specific transaction rules, water/septic/well, wildfire risk, short-term-rental permitting, buyer-agency changes. There is no keyword/question inventory in the repo driving content against that gap, and no gate requiring one.
items.why_it_matters: Being crawlable and well-marked-up only wins the citation if the page contains the answer. The markup layer is ahead of the content layer here.

open_questions_for_owner: Bytespider (ByteDance/TikTok) is Allowed in robots.ts and 403'd by middleware. Which way do you want it — allow it through the middleware, or drop it from robots.ts so the two files agree?

The geo screen 403s CN/HK/RU/SG for any bot not in GOOD_BOT_RE, which currently includes Perplexity-User, YouBot, meta-externalagent, and Amazonbot. Add those four to the bypass, or accept losing their Singapore/HK egress?
Do you want the AI-referral breakdown rendered on the existing admin analytics page (the data is already loaded there and thrown away), or as its own dedicated panel?
Subdivision pages are the one geo tier with no verified FAQ or market Dataset. Worth bringing to city/community/neighborhood parity, or is the subdivision tier intentionally thin?

Beyond stat-driven FAQs, do you want a question inventory built (Oregon transaction process, water rights/septic, wildfire, STR permitting) to target the non-numeric questions AI assistants actually field about Central Oregon?
Is llms-full.txt worth building, or is the curated llms.txt sufficient?
